alternative_uses(k1).text: Owners can move covered units to uses the ceiling does not reach.

binding(k1).text: The ceiling binds: it is below the price the market would otherwise reach.

buyouts_limited(k1).text: Buyouts move fewer tenants than the cap keeps in place.

can_delay(k3).text: Eligible buyers knew of the payment before it started and could delay purchases.

can_organize(k1).text: The groups with a concentrated stake can organize and spend to keep or change the rule.

commutable(k1).text: Shut-out buyers can buy in a neighbouring market outside the rule's reach at a bearable cost.

counterfactual_catches_up(k1).text: Without the rule, the market price soon passes any raise made in the announcement window.

durable_assets(k1).text: The covered assets are durable and their supply expands slowly.

enforced(k1).text: The ceiling is enforced against most bound sellers.

evasion(k1).text: Some exchanges take place above the ceiling without being caught.

exit_process(k1).text: Moving covered units to an alternative use requires a permit or board process.

expected_to_last(k1).text: Buyers of the covered assets expect the rule to last for many years.

keepers_dominate(k1).text: Among all protected tenants, the fall in moves out of the area among keepers outweighs the rise among the displaced.

lockin_dominates(k1).text: The lock-in outweighs moves diverted out of the area by higher free rents.

nontransferable(k1).text: The protected buyers' right is tied to holding the tenancy and cannot be sold.

not_fully_captured(k3).text: Sellers do not capture the whole payment: the recipients' net price falls.

opportunities_need_move(k1).text: Some valued opportunities for the protected buyers would require giving up the covered unit.

qualifying_pays(k3).text: Some can meet the criteria at a cost below the payment's worth to them.

quality_adjustable(k1).text: Sellers have room to cut quality or maintenance above any enforced minimum.

quantity_expands(k3).text: At least one side can expand its quantity: more of the subsidized good is traded.

relet_obstructs(k1).text: Re-letting a vacated unit obstructs the owner's later move to an alternative use.

search_open(k1).text: Seekers find covered units by their own search: no public list or allocation rule assigns them.

selection_open(k1).text: Sellers may choose among applicants by criteria of their own.

seller_supply_slow(k3).text: The sellers' supply of the subsidized good cannot grow at once.

sellers_fewer_alternatives(k3).text: While supply is fixed, the sellers have clearly fewer alternatives than the recipients.

substitutes(k1).text: Uncovered units in the same market are close substitutes for covered ones.

substitutes_given_up(k3).text: Some recipients would otherwise have bought an unsubsidized good.

takeup(k3).text: Many eligible recipients value the payment above the cost of qualifying, and claim it.

window_repricing(k1).text: Enough contracts come up for repricing in the announcement window, and sellers can raise the price on them.

would_leave(k1).text: Without the rule some protected buyers would have left the area.

components.cap_unit: dollars per 30-day supply of insulin collected from a covered resident
source_sentences: Section 3 of the Act provides: "A pharmacy shall not collect from a covered resident more than $35 for each 30-day supply of insulin."
A covered resident is a resident who is uninsured or enrolled in a plan regulated under the insurance code.
The cap applies to insulin dispensed on prescription and binds every "pharmacy licensed by the Board of Pharmacy under chapter 18".
The Board of Pharmacy enforces the cap: a $1,000 fine for each overcharge, paid into the Fund; repeated violation may lead to suspension of a license or permit.
The Board is funded by license and permit fees; the Act gives it no new money.
The bill was introduced on 15 January 2027 and signed on 12 April 2027. The Act takes effect on 1 January 2028.
Section 4(a) provides that the pharmacy bills the balance to the plan, "which shall pay it on the terms of its pharmacy contract".
Section 4(b) establishes the Insulin Access Fund, run by the Department of Health, for insulin fills of uninsured residents.
The Fund pays the pharmacy "the pharmacy's usual and customary price, less $35, but not more than the wholesale acquisition cost plus 20 percent, less $35".
The usual and customary price is "the price the pharmacy charges a cash-paying customer who is not a covered resident".
The uninsured resident attests at the pharmacy to having no coverage.
Section 6 provides that the Fund is paid "such sums as are necessary" from general revenue; fines under section 7 are paid into the Fund.
The bill was introduced on 15 January 2027 and signed on 12 April 2027. The Act takes effect on 1 January 2028.
The Department of Health runs the Fund through a claims contract (about $3 million a year, paid from the Fund).

context: Tarrenmoor has about 1,050 pharmacies licensed under chapter 18, section 18-4 (pharmacies located in the state), and about 140 nonresident permit holders under section 18-9.

About 70% of members of state-regulated plans pay more than $35 in a typical month; about 40% of uninsured cash buyers and 15% of high-deductible members said in a 2026 survey that they had used less insulin than prescribed because of cost.
List prices are set nationally by three manufacturers; the 58,000 users the Act reaches are about 0.7% of the national total.
